newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-MAINS REPEATS WORLD CUP POISONING CLAIM.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MAINS REPEATS WORLD CUP POISONING CLAIM.

text.p: Former New Zealand coach Laurie Mains repeated on Monday his claim that the All Blacks were poisoned before the World Cup final against South Africa last year.
Mains said in a television interview to launch his autobiography that a South African waitress named "Susie" was paid to poison the team on the eve of the final, won 15-12 by the Springboks.
He said he had discovered from two sources that the team's tea and coffee had been spiked.
Mains said he used his own money to hire a South African private investigator to find out what had happened to make almost all the New Zealand touring party sick before the match.
A handful of players were unaffected by the illness after arriving late for a meal and drinking freshly made tea or coffee.
"I just knew this was no case of ordinary old food poisoning," he said. "We were very, very sick, all but about four or five members of the whole touring party.

"I could never sleep after we came home from the World Cup. I felt until the day I died I was going to wonder what happened to us. I wasn't going to rest until I'd given it my best shot to find out what happened."
